6805 bearing support

Independent assembly · 4 mm wall · Existing 40 mm travel screw + bearing ring

100%

Motor screws lift off their flanges and move out through the side windows. The motor and wall separate next. The screw withdraws toward the motor side through the bearing, then the bearing leaves the rear recess. Loosen the coupling before disassembly.

The bearing carries axial load into the wall. The existing D-shaft clamp remains accessible through the open holder.

6805
4mm
30.3mm
Rear

Bearing behind the holder

The 6805 sits in a recess on the motor-facing side of the holder. Feed the threaded end of the screw through the bearing and the holder from the motor side; the printed shoulder rests against the inner race. The front lip of the holder supports the outer race. Four exposed mounting flanges and 9 mm side openings let you place the M3 screws directly on their seats. The supporting ribs sit above and below the screw heads, leaving the original coupling accessible.

Existing screw + bearing ring

The original helix, D bore and bolt/nut pockets are retained. The added ring has a Ø24.9 mm journal and Ø27 mm shoulder, occupying X22.3–31.3 mm. The coupling split stays open through the added material.

1 mm shorter holder

The holder projects 30.3 mm from the front of the 4 mm wall, reduced from 31.3 mm. The motor and screw keep their existing relative positions. The wall remains 52 × 52 × 4 mm. This separate prototype does not change the existing actuators.

Motor-facing recess

The bearing recess is Ø37.2 mm. Its forward lip contacts only the outer race, with 0.1 mm nominal axial clearance. The rear bearing-loading path stays clear. Rounded mounting flanges keep the original 6 mm stack and four M3×16 screws; no additional hardware is needed. Thrust toward the screw tip passes into the wall; reverse-direction retention relies on the coupling.

Geometry checks

Loading validation…

All 41 sampled exploded-assembly poses are free of solid intersections. Continuous insertion envelopes also verify side-loading and seating of each M3 screw, with 0.5 mm radial allowance around its head. The bearing leaves from the motor side; it never passes through the holder’s front lip. Sampling checks rigid clearances, not installation forces.

The intended load is about 1 lb (4.45 N static), not a tested capacity. CAD checks do not establish PETG creep life, fatigue or vibration resistance. Bearing internals are reference envelopes. This bearing does not prevent back-driving when the motor is unpowered.

Geometry report · Assembly pose report

Assembly and hardware

  1. Seat the 6805 in the recess on the motor-facing side of the holder.
  2. Feed the screw’s threaded end through the bearing and holder from the motor side, until its shoulder reaches the bearing’s inner race. Fit the original clamp nut and bolt loosely.
  3. Fit the 4 mm wall and motor, engaging the D shaft in the screw’s coupling. Place the four M3×16 screws through the side openings, then slide them axially into the exposed flange holes to fasten the holder and wall. Verify the motor accepts 6 mm thread engagement.
  4. Tighten the coupling through the open holder. Check free rotation and bearing seating before loading the prototype.

Print the wall flat; print the holder with its front face on the bed and standoffs upward. Check actual PETG fits before loading. Full build notes and hardware list.

Bearing dimensions: NSK 6805.
